text: Of David. I thank you with all my heart; before the gods I sing your praise.[footnote: Hebrew elohim; possibly "the heavenly beings" or "the mighty ones"]

versions.text: Of David. I thank you with all my heart; before the gods I sing your praise.
versions.explanation: "Before the gods" can be misread as acknowledging rival deities. A brief footnote noting the alternative senses of elohim (heavenly beings, mighty ones/rulers) would prevent confusion while keeping the current wording.

text: I bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness, for you have exalted your word above all your name.
On the day I called, you answered me; you made me bold, with strength in my soul.

versions.text: On the day I called, you answered me; you gave me strength and made me bold.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew בְנַפְשִׁי ("in my soul/within me") is dropped in the current rendering; restoring it keeps the inward dimension of the strengthening without harming the rhythm.

text: All the kings of the earth will thank you, LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth.

versions.text: All the kings of the earth will thank you, LORD, when they hear the words of your mouth.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כִּי שָׁמְעוּ is a causal clause with a perfect verb ("for they have heard"), not a temporal clause ("when they hear"). The current rendering turns a stated reason into a future condition and weakens the logic of the verse.

text: They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.
For the LORD is exalted, yet he sees the lowly; the proud he knows from afar.

versions.text: Though the LORD is exalted, he looks upon the lowly; the proud he knows from afar.
versions.explanation: The verse opens with כִּי ("for"), linking it to the greatness of the LORD's glory in verse 5; rendering it "Though" severs that connection and also repeats the same opening word as verse 7, which is monotonous when read aloud.

text: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you keep me alive; you stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand saves me.
The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me. Your steadfast love, LORD, endures forever—do not abandon the work of your hands.
